subject: Detection history for multispecies occupancy models

messages.author: 2044e4525a513916
messages.subject: Detection history for multispecies occupancy models
parts:
Hello everyone!

I am working on the camera trap-based species richness and its relation to anthropogenic and environmental covariates in a ~11,000 sqkm human-dominated forested landscape, with the help of multi-species occupancy models. However, due to logistic constraints, camera traps were not deployed simultaneously or at one go to cover the entire study area. Instead, there were multiple blocks in different time periods, and it took ~1.5 years to complete the survey. Since I have different record tables for different blocks, I wondered how to create a single list of detection history from these multiple record tables to run the multispecies occupancy models. Or is there any other way to address this issue? 
In this context, any suggestion/guidance is highly appreciated.

Thank you in advance!

Cheers
Sankarshan

messages.author: 2044e4525a513916
messages.subject: Re: Detection history for multispecies occupancy models
parts:
Additionally, after merging two or more record tables, I am also getting the following error repeatedly while creating the list of detection history for multispecies occupancy models:

"Error in cleanSubsetSpecies(subset_species2 = subset_species, stationCol2 = stationCol,  :
  No more records left. The detection history would be empty.
In addition: There were 30 warnings (use warnings() to see them)"

Where exactly am I doing it wrong? Is it due to combining two separate record tables, or is there any other issue?

Thanks in advance!

Sankarshan

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: Detection history for multispecies occupancy models
parts:
Hello, 
Normally it should be possible to simply combine the record tables with rbind(). Assuming you also have a camera operation matrix containing all stations, you should then be able to use detectionHistory() like normal for individual species.

To create detection histories for all species in a list you can call detection history within lapply(). Vignette 5 has examples. 

Regarding your error message, can you please share str() of the record table and the R code of your call to detectionHistory() you used? Also make sure that there are no typos in the species names.

Thank you

So far, I have used camera trap effort as detection covariate.

Thank you.
Regards
